title: Validated original-source interval at d=17 unconditional row
question: Can the exact finite R-419 oscillator/Hamiltonian source be enclosed at the larger cutoff d=17 and propagated through a fixed normalized one-site Gibbs row and residual compression?
method: Hash-pin the R-419 fixture and R-433 interval primitives, and fix V=2, d=17, beta=8, right orientation and emission ordinal zero before interval evaluation.
Assemble the exact rational finite source, split exchange/global-parity sectors into dimensions 81, 64, 72 and 72, and compute 50-digit point eigendata.

Use directed source intervals, residual/Gram bounds, polar correction and Gibbs-kernel propagation, then normalize the unconditional one-site marginal and enforce the fixed core/tail split at threshold four.
Project the coordinate momentum, build the 15-dimensional two-block residual compression, and certify a lower Cholesky probe, an upper Rayleigh probe and a rejection probe.
Run a non-importing NumPy control, hostile finite-scope mutations and Lean scalar cross-checks through the integrated verifier.
finding: The primary lane passes 57/57. The d=17 source residual and Gram upper bounds are 6.5554215021810497917e-41 and 6.2013656081312960463e-42. The normalized unconditional row is positive, its interval tail split is core 4..12 and tail 0..3,13..16, and the 15-dimensional residual interval has maximum entry width 7.0922943110070923e-13. The interval Rayleigh enclosure is [4.22153907112994631455003390284897397097200231, 4.22153907112994631578208377835242264266111368], strictly between probes 4.2 and 4.25; the 4.3 Cholesky probe is rejected. The independent non-importing control passes 12/12 with gap 4.221539067848923, the hostile lane rejects 8/8 mutations, the integrated verifier passes 15/15 and Lean R435 compiles.
decision_reason: Advance one larger-cutoff original-source interval datapoint at T0. The interval and independent controls are consistent, but the result remains finite and claim-nonbearing; residual reuse, all uniformities, common-core completion, physical reference and continuum gates remain open.
decision_scope: One V=2, d=17, beta=8, right-orientation unconditional one-site marginal (emission ordinal zero) from the exact R-419 rational source, with fixed threshold-four split and 15-dimensional residual interval compression.
boundary: R-435 is a finite source-interval certificate only. It does not close residual reuse, a common Q3 core, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a physical sector, a continuum limit, or any physical-empty, Yang-Mills or mass-gap claim.
next_action: Repeat at an independently fixed larger volume/cutoff with a predeclared row rule and owner-approved tail modulus; do not infer uniformity from the d=16 and d=17 datapoints.

adversarial_review.check: The manifest fixes beta 8, right orientation and ordinal zero before interval evaluation; no gap-based row optimization is allowed.
Source residual, Gram, polar, normalization and threshold intervals pass with directed arithmetic and explicit budgets.
The residual interval width and bracket are below fixed finite thresholds and the independent control is separate from the interval certificate.
Eight mutations covering aliasing, threshold/probe relaxation, cutoff substitution and promotion are rejected.
No common core, physical reference, Reading-H tangent or limit theorem is supplied.

no_overclaim: R-435 advances only one finite d=17 original-source interval certificate. It does not establish cutoff/volume uniformity, physical-empty sign, stationarity, transverse stability, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills dynamics or a mass gap.
